title: Conduct Risk and Consumer Outcomes
summary: The compliance function's role in identifying conduct risk, overseeing fair treatment of customers and testing whether the firm delivers good outcomes in practice.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: The compliance function's role in identifying conduct risk, overseeing fair treatment of customers and testing whether the firm delivers good outcomes in practice.
Learning Objectives: Explain the drivers of conduct risk and how they link to customer harm
Assess product governance, communications and complaints data for signs of poor outcomes
Design outcome testing that compliance can run alongside the business
Syllabus: Conduct risk drivers: business model, incentives and culture
Fair treatment, vulnerable customers and product governance
Complaints, root cause analysis and outcome indicators
Case study: spotting poor customer outcomes in management information
Intended Audience: Heads of compliance, compliance officers and deputies in regulated firms
Compliance analysts and monitoring staff moving into more senior or advisory roles
Risk, legal and business managers who work closely with the compliance function
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of working in or alongside a compliance function in a regulated firm is helpful. No legal qualification is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, Compliance and the Compliance Function in Banks (2005)
IOSCO, Compliance Function at Market Intermediaries (2006)
FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)
